sections.title: Form and origin
sections.text: Musa basjoo is a large rhizomatous herb native to southern China, despite its common name Japanese banana. Its pseudostems are about 2.5–4 m tall; a cultivated clump can spread 1.8–4.3 m.

sections.title: Leaves and fruit
sections.text: The large leaves often tear, and the inflorescence bracts hang down. The yellow-green fruits are about 5–10 cm long; their white flesh is sparse and contains many seeds.

sections.title: Use
sections.text: This species is mainly grown as an ornamental or for its fibres. NC State Extension does not consider the fruits edible.
